author: Plato
title: The Republic of Plato
edition: Benjamin Jowett translation, The Republic of Plato: An Ideal Commonwealth, revised edition (The Colonial Press, copyright 1901; Wikisource scan index identifies London, 1901). Translation year identifies this printed English edition, not Jowett’s first translation. Direct scan-backed Wikisource transcription of Books VI–VII; no Lawton introduction, illustration captions, or Jowett introductory matter is included. Prose wrapping is collapsed within preserved paragraphs, HTML emphasis becomes plain text, and printed page numbers, footnote references, and zero-width page-boundary characters are omitted. Main-text wording, punctuation, and apparent source transcription errors are retained; no claim of a fresh complete print-image collation is made. The library text holds the whole dialogue, Books I to X, each under its printed book title, with the persons of the dialogue and every quotation; the frontispiece, title page, Lawton's Special Introduction, the Introduction subpage and the 117 footnotes are omitted. As in the nightly selections, the few quotations the transcription sets line by line (verse and the displayed proportion in Book VII) are folded into paragraphs like the prose.

rights.basis: This identified English Jowett edition bears The Colonial Press copyright 1901 and is linked to its complete scanned print witness. Its English text was published before 1931 and is public domain in the United States as of 2026; the rights claim does not rely on the ancient Greek original. No modern editorial material is included.

acquisition.method: Wikisource rendered page HTML (index.php action=render) for the ten book subpages in printed order, The Republic of Plato/Book 1 to Book 10 (revisions 10050435, 10050449, 10050452, 10050454, 10050424, 10074709, 11985126, 10368554, 12283625, 12283635); downloadSha256 is the SHA-256 of the ten responses concatenated in that order and downloadUrl the first of them. Only the transcluded scan text is used: Wikisource headers, page-number anchors, footnote markers and lists and zero-width page-boundary characters removed; the work title and each book's number and title became headings; everything else, including table rows of the persons list and centred or line-set quotations, became paragraphs with whitespace and line breaks collapsed to single spaces; emphasis flattened.
